priority.when: You have one preferred model and only want fallback on failure.
priority.avoid: You need request distribution across models.
priority.example: Primary coding model with cheaper backup for outages.

weighted.when: You need controlled traffic split across models.
weighted.avoid: You cannot maintain accurate weights over time.

round-robin.when: You want predictable and even distribution.
round-robin.avoid: Models differ too much in latency or cost.
round-robin.example: Same model on multiple accounts to spread throughput.

random.when: You want simple distribution with minimal setup.

least-used.when: You want adaptive balancing based on live demand.
least-used.avoid: Traffic is too low to benefit from usage balancing.
least-used.example: Mixed workloads where one model often gets overloaded.

cost-optimized.when: Cost reduction is your top priority.
cost-optimized.avoid: Pricing data is missing or outdated.
cost-optimized.example: Background or batch jobs where lower cost is preferred.

reset-aware.when: You route across multiple accounts with quota telemetry and different reset windows.
reset-aware.avoid: Quota telemetry is unavailable for most accounts.
reset-aware.example: Prefer a 60% weekly account resetting tomorrow over an 80% account resetting later.

strict-random.when: Use when you want perfectly even spread — each model used once before repeating.
strict-random.avoid: Avoid when models have different quality or latency and order matters.
strict-random.example: Example: Multiple accounts of the same model to distribute usage evenly.

p2c.when: Use when you want low-latency selection using Power-of-Two-Choices algorithm.
p2c.avoid: Avoid for small combos with 2 or fewer models — no benefit over round-robin.
p2c.example: Example: High-throughput inference across 4+ equivalent model endpoints.

context-relay.when: Use when long sessions must survive account rotation without losing the working context.
context-relay.avoid: Avoid when account switching is rare or when you do not want extra summarization requests.
context-relay.example: Example: Codex sessions that rotate across multiple accounts near quota exhaustion.

fill-first.when: Use when you want to fully exhaust one provider's quota before moving to the next.
fill-first.avoid: Avoid when you need request-level load balancing across providers.
fill-first.example: Example: Use all $200 Deepgram credits before falling back to Groq.

auto.when: Use when you need multi-factor scoring routing based on cost, latency, and quality.
auto.avoid: Avoid when you need strict priority ordering or historical persistence.
auto.example: Example: Balance requests across models with different strengths.

lkgp.when: Use when you want to route based on historical success rates and performance.
lkgp.avoid: Avoid when historical data is limited or unreliable.
lkgp.example: Example: Route to models with a good track record on specific tasks.

context-optimized.when: Use when you need to optimize context window usage across models.
context-optimized.avoid: Avoid when models have similar context lengths or tasks are simple.
context-optimized.example: Example: Distribute long conversations across models with larger context windows.

advancedHelp.maxRetries: How many retries are attempted before failing a request.
advancedHelp.retryDelay: Initial wait between retries. Higher values reduce burst pressure.
advancedHelp.healthcheck: Skips unhealthy models/providers from routing decisions.
advancedHelp.concurrencyPerModel: Max simultaneous requests allowed per model in round-robin.
advancedHelp.queueTimeout: How long a request can wait in queue before timing out.
advancedHelp.failoverBeforeRetry: When enabled, any upstream error triggers immediate failover to the next combo target, skipping all retries and fallback URLs.

advancedHelp.disableSessionStickiness: Rotate to a different connection on every request instead of pinning a whole conversation to one connection by the first-message hash. Overrides the global default. Leave on Inherit to preserve prompt-cache hits for multi-turn chats.

priority.title: Fail-safe baseline
priority.description: Use one primary model and keep fallback chain short and reliable.
priority.tip1: Put your most reliable model first.
priority.tip2: Keep 1-2 backup models with similar quality.
priority.tip3: Use safe retries to absorb transient provider failures.

weighted.title: Controlled traffic split
weighted.description: Great for canary rollouts and gradual migration between models.
weighted.tip2: Keep the total at 100% and auto-balance after changes.
weighted.tip3: Monitor success and latency before increasing canary weight.

round-robin.title: Predictable load sharing
round-robin.description: Best when models are equivalent and you need smooth distribution.
round-robin.tip2: Set concurrency limits to avoid burst overload.
round-robin.tip3: Use queue timeout to fail fast under saturation.

random.title: Quick spread with low setup
random.description: Use when you need simple distribution without strict guarantees.
random.tip1: Use models with similar latency profiles.
random.tip2: Keep retries enabled to absorb random misses.
random.tip3: Prefer this for experimentation, not strict SLAs.

least-used.title: Adaptive balancing
least-used.description: Routes to less-used models to reduce hotspots over time.
least-used.tip2: Combine with health checks for safer balancing.
least-used.tip3: Track per-model usage to validate distribution gains.

cost-optimized.title: Budget-first routing
cost-optimized.description: Routes to lower-cost models when pricing metadata is available.
cost-optimized.tip1: Ensure pricing coverage for all selected models.
cost-optimized.tip2: Keep a quality fallback for hard prompts.
cost-optimized.tip3: Use for batch/background jobs where cost is the main KPI.

reset-aware.title: Reset-aware account rotation
reset-aware.description: Balances remaining provider quota against reset timing.
reset-aware.tip1: Use explicit account steps or account-tag routing for providers with quota telemetry.
reset-aware.tip2: Tune session vs weekly weights when short-term exhaustion is more risky.
reset-aware.tip3: Keep the tie band small so equivalent accounts still rotate fairly.

strict-random.title: Shuffle deck distribution
strict-random.description: Each model is used exactly once per cycle before reshuffling.
strict-random.tip1: Use at least 2 models for meaningful distribution.
strict-random.tip3: Ideal for load balancing across multiple API accounts.

fill-first.description: Exhaust provider quotas sequentially before falling back.
fill-first.tip1: Use for quota-based routing with clear fallback chains.
fill-first.tip2: Set quotas accurately to avoid premature fallback.

providers.grokRefreshIncluded: Refresh token included — automatic token renewal is enabled

providers.freeTierProvidersDesc: Providers with free tiers — some require an API key signup, others need no credentials at all.
providers.ideProvidersDesc: Editors with built-in AI subscription. Use the provider page to import credentials directly from the IDE keychain.
providers.noIdeProviders: No IDE providers match the current filters.
providers.providerDetailFastTierTooltip: Apply Codex Fast tier to all Codex connections by default
providers.webFetchTooltip: Providers that extract content from web URLs (HTML → Markdown, scrape, screenshot)
providers.compatibleProvidersDesc: OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible endpoints you host or configure. Point any OpenAI SDK to your own URL and route requests here.
providers.oauthProvidersDesc: Providers authenticated via OAuth — sign in once and TRouteAI handles token rotation automatically.
providers.webCookieProvidersDesc: These providers use browser web sessions, cookies, or web tokens instead of API keys. Open a provider to add the required session credential.
providers.apiKeyProvidersDesc: Standard API key providers. Add your key once and TRouteAI routes, retries, and rate-limits on your behalf.
providers.noAuthProvidersDesc: Open endpoints that require no credentials — ready to use immediately without any sign-up.
providers.upstreamProxyProvidersDesc: Route outbound traffic through an upstream proxy before it reaches the provider. Useful for corporate networks or traffic inspection.
providers.webFetchProvidersDesc: Providers that fetch and extract content from web URLs. Use them to ground prompts with live web data.
providers.aggregatorsGatewaysDesc: Multi-provider aggregators and AI gateways that expose a single unified API across dozens of underlying models.
providers.enterpriseCloudDesc: Enterprise-tier and cloud-hosted models with enhanced SLAs, compliance certifications, and dedicated capacity.
providers.cloudAgentProvidersDesc: Autonomous cloud agents that execute long-running tasks with plan approval and live status tracking.
providers.localProvidersDesc: Self-hosted models running on your own hardware. No data leaves your infrastructure.
providers.searchProvidersDesc: Web and document search providers. Attach them to LLM calls for Retrieval-Augmented Generation.
providers.audioProvidersDesc: Text-to-speech and speech-to-text providers for voice I/O and audio transcription pipelines.
providers.embeddingRerankProvidersDesc: Vector embedding and reranking providers for semantic search, RAG pipelines, and similarity scoring.
providers.imageProvidersDesc: Image generation and vision providers — create images from text or analyse existing ones.
providers.videoProvidersDesc: Video generation providers. Create short video clips from text prompts or images.
providers.onboardingWizardDescription: Connect API-key, custom compatible, and OAuth providers with validation, persistence, and an immediate connection test.
providers.onboardingTypeApiKeyText: Use built-in providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, Azure, and more.
providers.onboardingTypeCustomText: Create an OpenAI-, Anthropic-, or Claude Code-compatible endpoint and add its key.
providers.onboardingTypeOAuthText: Reuse the existing OAuth, device-code, or local import flows for coding providers.
providers.onboardingChooseProviderDescription: Select a provider, then the wizard will guide you through credentials and testing.
providers.onboardingOAuthNoConnectionFound: OAuth finished, but no provider connection was found.
providers.onboardingCreateCustomCompatibleDescript: The wizard creates a provider node first, then stores and tests its API-key connection.
providers.onboardingProviderPrefixHint: Used to generate the managed provider id.

onboardingProviderDescriptions.agentrouter: Get $200 free credits at https://agentrouter.org/register — no credit card required.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.aimlapi: Free tier paused (2026) — AI/ML API is now pay-as-you-go only (min $20 top-up); no recurring free credits.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.ai21: $10 trial credits on signup (valid 3 months), no credit card required
onboardingProviderDescriptions.alibaba: Connect Alibaba with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.alibaba-cn: Connect Alibaba (China) with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.bailian-coding-plan: Connect Alibaba Coding Plan with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.bedrock: Native Bedrock integration: model discovery uses Bedrock foundation models and inference profiles, while chat uses the regional Bedrock Runtime Converse/ConverseStream APIs.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.anthropic: Connect Anthropic with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.ant-ling: Register and create an API key at the Ant Ling API console (https://chat.ant-ling.com/open), then paste it here. TRouteAI routes chat traffic to https://api.ant-ling.com/v1/chat/completions; the provider is OpenAI-compatible and also exposes an Anthropic-compatible surface.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.api-airforce: Get your API key from https://panel.api.airforce — OpenAI-compatible endpoint at https://api.airforce/v1
onboardingProviderDescriptions.azure-ai: Foundry uses the OpenAI v1 surface with deployment names as models. TRouteAI normalizes root resource URLs to the v1 chat and /models endpoints.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.azure-openai: Use your Azure OpenAI API key. Base URL should be your resource endpoint, for example https://my-resource.openai.azure.com.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.bai: Bearer API key for the b.ai OpenAI-compatible LLM gateway (distinct from TheB.AI). Create a key at https://docs.b.ai, then use https://api.b.ai/v1 as the OpenAI-compatible base URL.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.qianfan: Use a Qianfan API key from Baidu AI Cloud. The default endpoint is OpenAI-compatible v2.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.baseten: $30 free trial credits for GPU inference
onboardingProviderDescriptions.bazaarlink: Create a free API key at https://bazaarlink.ai — model 'auto:free' routes to zero-cost inference. All models use the provider/model-name format, e.g. xiaomi/mimo-v2.5-pro.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.black-forest-labs: Connect Black Forest Labs with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.blackbox: Free tier: unlimited basic chat plus Minimax-M2.5, no credit card required
onboardingProviderDescriptions.bluesminds: Get your API key at https://www.bluesminds.com — OpenAI-compatible endpoint at https://api.bluesminds.com/v1 with free daily credits. VIP models (Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Pro) consume pi credits.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.byteplus: Connect BytePlus ModelArk with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.cerebras: Free Trial: 1M tokens/day, 30K TPM, 5 RPM — no credit card.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.charm-hyper: Create an API key at https://hyper.charm.land, then paste it here as a Bearer token.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.chutes: Bearer API key for the Chutes OpenAI-compatible gateway.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.clarifai: Clarifai exposes OpenAI-compatible chat, responses and /models on /v2/ext/openai/v1. Public/community models typically require a PAT; app-scoped keys only work for resources inside that app.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.cloudflare-ai: Requires API Token AND Account ID (found at dash.cloudflare.com)
onboardingProviderDescriptions.clova-studio: CLOVA Studio (HyperCLOVA X) is OpenAI-compatible on /v1/openai. TRouteAI probes /v1/openai/models and routes chat traffic to /v1/openai/chat/completions. Uses the current clovastudio.stream.ntruss.com host — the legacy clovastudio.apigw.ntruss.com endpoint is being deprecated.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.codestral: Connect Codestral with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.cohere: Free Trial: 1,000 API calls/month for testing, no credit card required
onboardingProviderDescriptions.command-code: Create or copy an API key from Command Code, then paste it here as a Bearer token.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.crof: Connect CrofAI with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.databricks: Connect Databricks with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.datarobot: The default gateway catalogs active models from /genai/llmgw/catalog/. Deployment URLs are also supported for direct OpenAI-compatible chat requests.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.deepinfra: Free signup credits for API testing and model exploration
onboardingProviderDescriptions.deepseek: 5M free tokens on signup - no credit card required
onboardingProviderDescriptions.dgrid: Create a DGrid API key at https://dgrid.ai, then use https://api.dgrid.ai/v1 as the OpenAI-compatible base URL.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.dify: Get API key from your Dify instance.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.digitalocean: Connect DigitalOcean with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.dit: dit.ai (Distributed Intelligence Trade) is an OpenAI-compatible router/gateway with dynamic per-request pricing, exposing /v1/chat/completions at https://api.dit.ai/v1. TRouteAI uses the OpenAI protocol; spend/savings analytics live in the dit.ai dashboard.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.empower: Empower exposes OpenAI-compatible chat on https://app.empower.dev/api/v1 with tool-calling support on empower-functions.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.factory: Get your Factory API key at https://app.factory.ai/settings/api-keys, then paste it as a Bearer token. OpenAI-compatible endpoint at https://api.factory.ai/v1.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.fal-ai: Connect Fal.ai with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.featherless-ai: Free tier available — no credit card required
onboardingProviderDescriptions.fenayai: Bearer API key for the FenayAI OpenAI-compatible gateway.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.firecrawl: Connect Firecrawl with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.fireworks: $1 free starter credits on signup for API testing
onboardingProviderDescriptions.freeaiapikey: Discounted API proxy for 40+ models including GPT-5, Claude Opus 4.6, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Qwen 3.5. Get your API key at https://freeaiapikey.com/dashboard. Base URL: https://freeaiapikey.com/v1.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.freemodel-dev: Get $300 free API credits at https://freemodel.dev — no payment info required. OpenAI-compatible endpoint. GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.5 models available.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.friendliai: Free tier for serverless inference — no credit card required
onboardingProviderDescriptions.gemini: Free forever: 1,500 req/day for Gemini 2.5 Flash — no credit card, get key at aistudio.google.com
onboardingProviderDescriptions.gigachat: Connect GigaChat (Sber) with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.github-models: Create a GitHub PAT with 'models: read' scope at github.com/settings/tokens
onboardingProviderDescriptions.gitlab: GitLab personal access token for the public Code Suggestions API. Configure a self-hosted base URL when not using gitlab.com.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.gitlawb-gmi: Get your API key from Gitlawb Opengateway dashboard.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.gitlawb: Get your API key from Gitlawb Opengateway dashboard.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.glm: Connect GLM Coding with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.glm-cn: Connect GLM Coding (China) with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.glmt: Preset GLM profile with higher token budget, thinking enabled, and longer timeout.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.getgoapi: Connect GoAPI with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.groq: Free tier: 30 RPM / 14.4K RPD — no credit card
onboardingProviderDescriptions.hackclub: Sign in with your Hack Club account at ai.hackclub.com.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.heroku: Connect Heroku AI with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.huggingface: Free Inference API for thousands of models (Whisper, VITS, SDXL…)
onboardingProviderDescriptions.hyperbolic: $1-5 trial credits on signup for serverless inference
onboardingProviderDescriptions.watsonx: The watsonx model gateway exposes OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions and /models under /ml/gateway/v1.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.inception: Inception Labs is OpenAI-compatible at https://api.inceptionlabs.ai/v1. mercury-2 is the first diffusion LLM (dLLM) in the catalog — 5-10x faster generation than comparable autoregressive models, with tool calling, json_mode, and structured outputs.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.inference-net: $25 free credits on signup plus research grants available
onboardingProviderDescriptions.internlm: Free monthly quota ~1M input / 3M output tokens (~10 RPM)
onboardingProviderDescriptions.jina-ai: Bearer API key for the Jina AI rerank API.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.jina-reader: Connect Jina Reader with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.kenari: Kenari exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint at https://kenari.id/v1/chat/completions, plus a live /v1/models catalog covering Claude, GPT, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi and more. TRouteAI uses the OpenAI protocol and lists models via passthrough.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.kie: Connect KIE.AI with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.kilo-gateway: Connect Kilo Gateway with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.kimi: Connect Kimi with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.kimi-coding-apikey: Connect Kimi Coding (API Key) with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.lambda-ai: Connect Lambda AI with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.laozhang: Connect LaoZhang AI with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.llamagate: Connect LlamaGate with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.llm7: Works without API key (use 'unused' as key). Get free token at token.llm7.io for higher limits.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.longcat: Free: one-time 10M-token grant after account signup + KYC verification (LongCat-2.0). One-time only — not a recurring daily/monthly allowance.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.maritalk: Connect Maritalk with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.meta-llama: Connect Meta Llama API with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.minimax-cn: Connect Minimax (China) with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.minimax: Connect Minimax Coding with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.mistral: Free Experiment tier: rate-limited access to all models, no credit card required
onboardingProviderDescriptions.modal: Modal commonly serves user-hosted OpenAI-compatible apps on /v1. TRouteAI will probe /v1/models and route chat traffic to /v1/chat/completions.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.modelscope: Free tier via ModelScope API-Inference — Alibaba account required.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.moonshot: Connect Kimi with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.nanogpt: Connect NanoGPT with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.nebius: ~$1 trial credits on signup for API testing
onboardingProviderDescriptions.nlpcloud: NLP Cloud uses a proprietary chatbot API instead of OpenAI chat/completions. TRouteAI adapts OpenAI messages to input/context/history and exposes a local catalog of supported chatbot models.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.nous-research: Nous exposes an OpenAI-compatible /v1 surface with a large remote /models catalog. The /chat/completions endpoint requires a valid API key for programmatic inference.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.novita: $0.50 trial credits on signup (valid about 1 year)
onboardingProviderDescriptions.nscale: $5 free credits on signup for inference testing
onboardingProviderDescriptions.nube: Connect Nube.sh with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.nvidia: Free dev access: ~40 RPM, 70+ models (Kimi K2.5, GLM 4.7, DeepSeek V3.2...)
onboardingProviderDescriptions.oci: OCI exposes OpenAI-compatible chat and responses endpoints. Project ID is optional in TRouteAI but may be required for Responses and agentic workflows.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.ollama-cloud: Connect Ollama Cloud with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.openadapter: OpenAdapter exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint at https://api.openadapter.in/v1/chat/completions, aggregating 70+ open-source models (DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, MiniMax, GLM, Llama, Mistral, …). TRouteAI uses the OpenAI protocol.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.openai: Connect OpenAI with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.opencode-go: Connect OpenCode Go with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.opencode-zen: Connect OpenCode Zen with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.openrouter: Free models at $0/token with :free suffix - 20 RPM / 200 RPD
onboardingProviderDescriptions.openvecta: Free credits on signup for OpenAI-compatible inference across LLMs, embeddings, and reasoning models
onboardingProviderDescriptions.orcarouter: Create an API key (starts with sk-orca-) at https://www.orcarouter.ai, then paste it as a Bearer token. OpenAI-compatible endpoint at https://api.orcarouter.ai/v1.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.ovhcloud: Connect OVHcloud AI with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.perplexity: Connect Perplexity with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.piapi: Connect PiAPI with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.pioneer: $75 free usage credits — no credit card required
onboardingProviderDescriptions.plamo: PLaMo is OpenAI-compatible at https://api.platform.preferredai.jp/v1. Built by Preferred Networks and optimized for Japanese. Docs are primarily in Japanese.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.poe: Poe exposes OpenAI-compatible chat and responses on https://api.poe.com/v1, with authenticated balance checks on /usage/current_balance.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.pollinations: Free keyless tier: openai, openai-fast, openai-large, qwen-coder, mistral, deepseek, grok, gemini-flash-lite-3.1, perplexity-fast, perplexity-reasoning. Premium models (claude, gemini, midijourney) require a Pollinations API key from enter.pollinations.ai.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.publicai: Requires an API key — one-time signup credit, then paid
onboardingProviderDescriptions.puter: Get token at puter.com/dashboard → Copy Auth Token
onboardingProviderDescriptions.qiniu: Create a Qiniu AI inference API key at https://portal.qiniu.com/ai-inference/api-key, then paste it here as a Bearer token. OpenAI-compatible endpoint at https://api.qnaigc.com/v1, proxying DeepSeek, Claude, Kimi and more behind one key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.recraft: Connect Recraft with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.reka: Reka Chat is OpenAI-compatible on /v1. TRouteAI probes /v1/models and routes chat traffic to /v1/chat/completions.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.requesty: Create an API key at https://app.requesty.ai, then paste it here as a Bearer token. OpenAI-compatible endpoint at https://router.requesty.ai/v1, with a live /v1/models catalog.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.runwayml: Runway video generation is task-based. TRouteAI submits text-to-video or image-to-video jobs, polls /v1/tasks/[id], and normalizes the finished video outputs back into the OpenAI-like /v1/videos/generations response.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.sambanova: $5 free credits on signup (30-day validity), no credit card required
onboardingProviderDescriptions.sap: Model discovery uses /v2/lm/scenarios/foundation-models/models on AI_API_URL. Chat requests use deploymentUrl/chat/completions and require AI-Resource-Group.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.sarvam: Sarvam AI is OpenAI-compatible on /v1. TRouteAI probes /v1/models and routes chat traffic to /v1/chat/completions. Models are tuned for Indic languages.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.scaleway: 1M free tokens for new accounts — EU/GDPR compliant (Paris), Qwen3 235B & Llama 70B
onboardingProviderDescriptions.siliconflow: $1 free credits plus permanently free models after identity verification
onboardingProviderDescriptions.snowflake: Connect Snowflake Cortex with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.stability-ai: Connect Stability AI with an API key.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.sumopod: SumoPod exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint at https://ai.sumopod.com/v1/chat/completions, plus a live /v1/models catalog. TRouteAI uses the OpenAI protocol and lists models via passthrough.
onboardingProviderDescriptions.suno: Paste session cookie from suno.ai (Clerk auth)
onboardingProviderDescriptions.synthetic: Connect Synthetic with an API key.

settings.routingSettingsIntro: Controls how your requests are routed, transformed, and sent to AI providers.
settings.routingOpDropParagraphContainsDesc: Removes any paragraph (text block split on blank lines) inside the system prompt whose text contains ANY of the listed substrings. Use to strip third-party client fingerprints like 'github.com/anomalyco/opencode' or 'docs.openwebui.com' that Anthropic's classifier flags.
settings.routingOpDropParagraphStartsWithDesc: Removes any paragraph that STARTS WITH one of the listed prefixes. Use for identity lines like 'You are OpenCode' or 'You are Open WebUI' that announce the calling client.
settings.routingOpReplaceTextDesc: Replaces a literal substring with another literal substring. Use for known trigger phrases — e.g. rewrite 'Here is some useful information about the environment you are running in:' to 'Environment context you are running in:' (an empirically-validated trigger phrase).
settings.routingOpReplaceRegexDesc: Replaces text matching a regular expression. Use when you need patterns (character classes, optional whitespace, anchors) instead of literal substrings. A malformed pattern is caught at runtime when the op runs.
settings.routingOpDropBlockContainsDesc: Removes ENTIRE system blocks (not just paragraphs) whose text contains any of the listed substrings. Use when a whole block is fingerprint-bearing and you want it gone — e.g. an injected MCP-server description.
settings.routingOpPrependSystemBlockDesc: Inserts a new text block at the FRONT of the system array. Use to add the SDK identity 'You are a Claude agent, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK.' that Anthropic's classifier expects.
settings.routingOpAppendSystemBlockDesc: Inserts a new text block at the END of the system array. Use for cosmetic additions that don't need to be at position [0].
settings.routingOpInjectBillingHeaderDesc: Prepends the special 'x-anthropic-billing-header: cc_version=...; cc_entrypoint=...; cch=...;' text block that Anthropic's classifier validates. Required for CC bridge relay endpoints; for the native claude provider TRouteAI already injects its own billing line so this op is usually redundant there.
settings.routingOpObfuscateWordsDesc: Inserts a Zero-Width-Joiner character after the first letter of each listed word, so 'opencode' becomes 'o‍pencode'. Reads identical to humans but bypasses classifier word matches. Targets system blocks, user/assistant messages, and tool descriptions.
settings.routingNeedlesHint: List of substrings. A paragraph matches if it contains ANY one of them. Add one per line via 'Add entry'.
settings.routingPrefixesHint: List of strings. A paragraph matches if it starts with any one of them (leading whitespace is trimmed before matching).
settings.routingCaseSensitiveHint: When ON, 'OpenCode' and 'opencode' are different strings. When OFF (default), the comparison ignores case.
settings.routingMatchLiteralHint: Exact literal substring to find. No regex syntax — special chars like . * ? are treated as themselves.
settings.routingReplacementTextHint: Replacement string. Leave blank to delete the match. The output preserves surrounding text.
settings.routingAllOccurrencesHint: When ON (default), every instance is replaced. When OFF, only the first match is replaced.
settings.routingPatternHint: JavaScript regex source. Don't wrap in slashes — just 'foo(.*)bar'. Server rejects patterns that fail to compile.
settings.routingRegexFlagsHint: JavaScript regex flags (g = all matches, i = case-insensitive, s = dot matches newline, m = multiline). Default 'g'.
settings.routingBlockTextHint: Full text of the new system block. Use a literal string; the system block stores text only.
settings.routingIdempotencyKeyHint: Optional. If set, the op skips when a block whose text starts with this key is already present. Prevents double-prepend on retries.
settings.routingBillingEntrypointHint: Value injected as 'cc_entrypoint='. Anthropic accepts 'sdk-cli' (Agent SDK), 'cli' (Claude Code CLI), or other documented values.
settings.routingBillingVersionFormatHint: How the 3-char build hash after cc_version= is computed. 'ex-machina' = sha256 of CCH_SALT+chars-from-first-user-msg+version (per-message). 'trouteai-daystamp' = sha256 of YYYY-MM-DD+version (stable per-day).
settings.routingBillingCchAlgoHint: How the 5-char cch= token is computed. 'sha256-first-user' = sha256 of first user message text. 'xxhash64-body' = body-level signing fills it later. 'static-zero' = literal '00000' placeholder.
settings.routingObfuscateWordsHint: Lowercase words to obfuscate. ZWJ insertion is applied case-insensitively, so 'opencode' also matches 'OpenCode' and 'OPENCODE'.
settings.routingObfuscateTargetsHint: Which body regions to scan for the words: system blocks, user/assistant messages, and/or tool descriptions.

settings.resilienceRequestQueueEffect: Queues requests, limits concurrency, and spaces out calls
settings.resilienceRequestQueueDesc: This layer only controls queueing and pacing. It does not store cooldowns or open circuit breakers.
settings.resilienceAutoEnableApiKeyProvidersDesc: Enables queue protection by default for active API key connections.
settings.resilienceConnectionCooldownTrigger: When a connection returns a transient upstream failure
settings.resilienceConnectionCooldownEffect: Temporarily skips that connection and increases backoff for repeated failures
settings.resilienceConnectionCooldownDesc: The base cooldown covers transient connection failures. When upstream retry hints are enabled, the provider's explicit window overrides the local cooldown.
settings.resilienceUseUpstreamRetryHintsDesc: Uses retry-after/reset values from the upstream provider when available.
settings.resilienceUseUpstream429BreakerHints: Use upstream 429 hints for breaker cooldown
settings.resilienceUseUpstream429BreakerHintsDesc: Apply Retry-After / quota-exhausted signals from 429 responses to the circuit-breaker cooldown duration. Default uses a per-provider policy: direct cloud providers default on; reverse-proxy, self-hosted, and CLI-backed providers default off. Independent of "Use upstream retry hints".
settings.resilienceProviderBreakerTrigger: Final transport/server failures after connection fallback is exhausted
settings.resilienceProviderBreakerEffect: Temporarily blocks that provider until the reset time expires
settings.resilienceProviderBreakerDesc: Live breaker state appears only on the Health page. Connection-scoped 429 rate limits stay in Connection Cooldown and do not trip the provider breaker.
settings.resilienceWaitForCooldownTrigger: When all candidate connections are already cooling down
settings.resilienceWaitForCooldownEffect: Waits on the server and retries when the first cooldown expires
settings.resilienceWaitForCooldownDesc: This only affects the current request. It does not store connection or provider state.
settings.resilienceEnableServerWaitDesc: When enabled, TRouteAI waits for the first cooldown to expire and retries automatically.
settings.resilienceComboCooldownWaitDesc: For all combo strategies: wait out a short transient cooldown and re-dispatch instead of returning a 429 immediately. Never waits on quota_exhausted.
settings.resilienceComboCooldownWaitToggleDesc: All combo strategies; never waits on quota_exhausted.
settings.resilienceQuotaShareConcurrencyDesc: For quota-share combos only: when a connection sets a Max Concurrent cap, serialize concurrent requests to that subscription account so it is never flooded past its ceiling. Excess requests wait in the queue instead of getting a 429. The cap comes from each connection's Max Concurrent field; this switch only enables or disables honoring it.
settings.resilienceQuotaShareConcurrencyToggleDes: Quota-share combos only; honors each connection's Max Concurrent cap.
settings.resilienceProviderCooldownEffect: Skips the failed provider for a cooldown period before retrying
settings.resilienceProviderCooldownDesc: Prevents subsequent requests from re-walking the same failing providers. Cooldown scales exponentially with consecutive failures.
settings.resilienceProviderCooldownEnabledDesc: When enabled, failed providers are tracked globally and skipped for a cooldown period.
settings.forcedFingerprintTitle: Always enabled for {provider} — required for OAuth account safety; cannot be turned off.
settings.sessionAffinityDesc: Keeps one conversation on the same account for this many seconds, for any provider. 0 disables it.
settings.resetAwareQuotaCacheDesc: Caches quota telemetry for reset-aware ordering only. Quota preflight still protects requests. 0/0 keeps live fetching.

settings.denoRelayFreeTierNote: Deno Deploy v2 runs on a global edge network. Free tier: 1M requests & 100GiB outbound traffic per month, no per-request CPU limits, up to 20 active apps & 50 custom domains.

settings.cloudflareRelayAccountIdHint: Found on the right side of the Cloudflare dashboard overview page.
settings.cloudflareRelayApiTokenHint: Requires 'Workers Scripts: Edit' permission. The token is used only at deploy time and is never stored.
settings.cloudflareRelayFreeTierNote: Free tier: 100,000 requests/day per Cloudflare account.

oauthModal.loopbackMismatchExplanation: After you approve the login, {providerName} always sends the browser back to {redirectUri}. That address points at the computer running this browser, not at the TRouteAI server — so the authorization code never reaches TRouteAI and the provider fails the sign-in without showing an error.
oauthModal.loopbackMismatchStep1: On this computer, open a terminal and start an SSH tunnel to the TRouteAI server:
oauthModal.loopbackMismatchStep1Note: Replace {userPlaceholder} with your SSH username. Keep this terminal open until the connection shows as active — both ports are needed: one serves the dashboard, the other receives the callback.
oauthModal.loopbackMismatchStep2: In this browser, reopen TRouteAI through the tunnel:
oauthModal.loopbackMismatchStep3: Then connect {providerName} again from the new tab. The callback now reaches the server and the login completes normally.

REQUIRE_API_KEY.description: Require an API key for all incoming requests.

INPUT_SANITIZER_ENABLED.description: Enable input sanitization for all requests.

PII_REDACTION_ENABLED.description: Redact personally identifiable information from requests.

PII_RESPONSE_SANITIZATION.description: Sanitize personally identifiable information in provider responses.

PII_RESPONSE_SANITIZATION_MODE.description: Choose how response PII is handled: redact replaces it, warn only logs it, block rejects the response, and off disables sanitization.

OUTBOUND_SSRF_GUARD_ENABLED.description: Block outbound requests to private or internal IP ranges.

ALLOW_API_KEY_REVEAL.description: Allow authenticated dashboard users to reveal stored API keys instead of seeing masked values only.

PROXY_AUTO_SELECT_ENABLED.description: When no proxy is assigned to a connection, automatically select the first working registry proxy. Off by default because otherwise one registry proxy becomes a global fallback for all traffic.

TROUTEAI_CONTROL_PLANE_PROXY_DIRECT_FALL.description: Allow OAuth and provider-validation flows to bypass a pinned proxy when proxy reachability checks fail. Off by default because this can change the account egress IP.

MITM_DISABLE_TLS_VERIFY.description: Disable TLS certificate verification for the MITM proxy.

TROUTEAI_ALLOW_PRIVATE_PROVIDER_URLS.description: Allow provider URLs that point to private or internal networks.

TROUTEAI_ALLOW_LOCAL_PROVIDER_URLS.description: Allow providers on localhost, LAN, and private IP ranges. This is required for local OpenAI-compatible models and enabled by default. Cloud-metadata endpoints such as 169.254.169.254 remain blocked.

TOOL_POLICY_MODE.description: Set the tool-use policy enforcement mode.

RATE_LIMIT_AUTO_ENABLE.description: Automatically enable rate limiting based on usage patterns.

ALLOW_MULTI_CONNECTIONS_PER_COMPAT_NODE.description: Allow multiple connections for each compatibility node.

RESPONSES_PASSTHROUGH_DROP_COMMENTARY.description: Remove internal commentary-phase output items from Responses API passthrough streams before forwarding them to clients. Disable this flag to receive raw upstream commentary.

TROUTEAI_MCP_ENFORCE_SCOPES.description: Enforce scope restrictions for MCP tool access.

TROUTEAI_MCP_COMPRESS_DESCRIPTIONS.description: Compress MCP tool descriptions to reduce token usage.

TROUTEAI_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_SERVICES.description: Disable all background services, including quota refresh and synchronization.

TROUTEAI_RTK_TRUST_PROJECT_FILTERS.description: Trust project-level RTK filters without validation.

TROUTEAI_ENABLE_LIVE_WS.description: Start the real-time dashboard WebSocket server on import at loopback port 20132. Set the flag to 0 or false to disable it. LAN exposure also requires LIVE_WS_HOST=0.0.0.0 and LIVE_WS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS.

TROUTEAI_CODEX_WS_ENABLED.description: Allow Codex to use Responses over WebSocket. When disabled, Codex falls back to HTTP Responses.

TROUTEAI_EMERGENCY_FALLBACK.description: Route budget-exhausted requests to the emergency free fallback provider and model.

STREAM_RECOVERY_ENABLED.description: Retry truncated upstream SSE streams transparently before any response bytes reach the client.

STREAM_RECOVERY_MIDSTREAM_ENABLED.description: Allow stream recovery to request the response again and stitch it after bytes have already reached the client.

MODEL_CATALOG_INCLUDE_NAMES.description: Include display-friendly name fields in /v1/models responses. Disable this for clients that accept model IDs only.

MODELS_CATALOG_PREFIX_MODE.description: Control model-ID prefixes in /v1/models: dual emits alias and canonical prefixes, alias emits short prefixes only, and canonical emits full provider IDs only.

ARENA_ELO_SYNC_ENABLED.description: Periodically synchronize Arena AI leaderboard ELO data for model-intelligence rankings.

CLI_COMPAT_ALL.description: Enable compatibility mode for all CLI clients.

PRICING_SYNC_ENABLED.description: Synchronize pricing data automatically. The PRICING_SYNC_ENABLED environment variable must also be true.

TROUTEAI_AUTO_SYNC_CODEX_PROFILES.description: After provider-model synchronization, regenerate ~/.codex/*.config.toml profiles from the live catalog. This never changes the active or default Codex configuration and is off by default.

TROUTEAI_AUTO_SYNC_CLAUDE_PROFILES.description: After provider-model synchronization, regenerate ~/.claude/profiles/<name>/settings.json profiles from the live catalog. This never changes the active or default Claude configuration and is off by default.
